title: The customer rings about the bill; the lead advisor owns the mistake and promises the senior's call
purpose: Story S8, the complaint. The car was a day late and the bill is not what was quoted. Travis does not argue the quote, explains the bill, says what he cannot decide himself and who will, and sums it up. It is a call about a job already done: two checks, no score.

mentioned.name: Ray Brennan
mentioned.role: the founder, named by the customer

call.day: the day the car is ready: the next full open day after slot 7's 4th working day before T on which slot 5 works (rule R6; card S08, call 10)

scenario.who_calls: Frank Daugherty, who argued at the counter that morning, left without paying and has had three hours to get angrier.
scenario.job: timing belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump, done; billed at list
scenario.wants: to pay what he was quoted
scenario.what_happens: Travis lets him finish, says the quote was the shop's mistake, breaks the bill down, says the same-day promise should not have been made, says he could match the quote himself but the lost day as well takes it past ten percent, which is the service manager's to decide, promises Greg's call before ten the next morning and sums up: who calls, when, where the car stays and what is being decided.

facts.note: 720.00 + shop supplies 21.60 = 741.60 before tax, 810.20 with sales tax (catalogue.json story_pins.S8). Matching the quote is 741.60 - 688.00 = 53.60 off, 7.2 % of the bill before tax, inside an advisor's 10 % (ledger price.discount_rule_pct); Travis escalates because the customer also lost a day, and anything past 10 % needs the senior's approval.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Travis.
Travis, this is Frank Daugherty. I was just in there this mornin' about my Subaru.
Yes sir, Mr. Daugherty. The Outback. I saw you at the counter with Caleb.
Then you know. I was told six hundred and eighty-eight dollars and I was told Monday. I come in there this mornin' — Tuesday — and that boy hands me a bill for eight hundred and ten.
Yes sir.
Now I don't know what kind of outfit quotes a man one price and charges him another, but I'm not payin' it. I've been bringin' cars to Ray Brennan since before you worked there.
I hear you. And I'm not gonna tell you you heard wrong, 'cause you didn't. Can I walk you through what happened, and then tell you what I'm gonna do about it?
Go ahead.

The price for that job is seven-twenty. It's been seven-twenty since our labor rate went up a few months back. Caleb read you six eighty-eight off a page that never got updated. That's our mistake, not yours.
Uh-huh.
And the rest of it?

The rest is shop supplies, twenty-one sixty, and sales tax. That's how seven-twenty turns into eight-ten out the door. It's like the menu price and the check — same meal, but nobody told you about the tax.
Nobody told me a lot of things. He told me same day.
Yes sir. He shouldn't have. That's better than a three-hour job, and we didn't get it on the lift till after lunch Monday.
So what are you gonna do?

Here's where I am. Matching the quote I could do myself, but you lost a day too, and anything past ten percent is Greg's — Greg Whitaker, our service manager. He's at the other shop today; I'm writing it up for him now, with the six eighty-eight you were quoted on it.
Uh-huh.
I'm not comin' back down there to argue.
You won't have to. Greg'll call you tomorrow morning, before ten. Is this the best number?
It's the only one I got.

Okay. So: Greg Whitaker calls you tomorrow before ten at this number. The Outback's done, and it stays locked up here at twenty-one-oh-six East Main tonight, no charge for that. And what he's deciding is the difference between the six eighty-eight you were told and the seven forty-one sixty on the bill.
Okay.
Alright. Before ten.
Before ten. And Mr. Daugherty — I'm sorry about this one.
Well. We'll see.
Yes sir. Talk to you tomorrow.
